"Iran says deal on Strait of Hormuz is close but will not open the waterway by itself" (NBC News / AP, Sat 8 Aug 2026)

Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi told reporters Saturday that Iran and Oman were "very close" to agreement on a new shipping route through the Strait of Hormuz — negotiators closing in on temporary lanes for ships entering and exiting the Persian Gulf.

Araghchi: "We are very close to an agreement."

But reopening the strait depends on other conditions. Araghchi said reopening was "subject to other conditions," including the United States making amends for what he said was a violation of the memorandum of understanding agreed between the two countries in June.

He singled out Article Five of the June MoU — which called on Iran to "make arrangements" for vessel transits through Hormuz — claiming the US undermined Tehran's management of the strait by seeking to establish its own alternative routes.

Bloomberg (8 Aug): "Iran Says Hormuz Deal Close But That Its Conditions Must Be Met." Any agreement won't result in an immediate reopening of the strait, signalling that any respite for energy supplies may be limited. Iran and Oman were discussing a temporary route because a permanent new route involves extensive technical and legal complexities.

Agreement over control of the waterway is seen as crucial to a wider deal to end the conflict that began with US and Israeli attacks on Iran on 28 February.
